transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-15 14:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Markus Chen (CTO, Klaxon), Lena Ortiz (Lead ML Engineer), Dina Patel (Security)

Summary (auto): High-level discovery about migrating from OpenAI-managed endpoints to Redwood Dedicated; Klaxon runs a mix of chat and embedding workloads with vLLM for local evaluation; main concerns are eval parity, request/response format compatibility, quantization effects, and enterprise security controls.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I think we got most of the group on, uh, curious who wants to kick off, Markus?
[00:12] Markus: Yeah, thanks. I'll start. We run Klaxon AI chat features in our product. Currently using OpenAI for hosted endpoints but the cost and some of the latency variability have been painful. We're evaluating options: keep using hosted OpenAI, maybe Anthropic for safety gains, or move to a Dedicated provider.
[00:28] Lena: And from infra/ML, we run a bunch of evals locally using vLLM and TGI stacks. We train/serve with a mixture of HF artifacts and some custom tokenizers; so compatibility is a big question.
[00:40] Jordan: Totally. Priya, do you want to give a quick overview of how Redwood handles compatibility and Dedicated?
[00:45] Priya: Sure. Quick note first — sorry for audio, I might be on a noisy connection. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, VPC peering, and a control plane that can be private. For compatibility, we support standard HF model formats and have been adding adapters for vLLM/TGI styles. That said, there are occasional tokenizer differences and kernel-level differences after quantization that we'll want to validate.
[01:10] Markus: When you say HF formats, do you mean we can bring the exact model artifacts we use in vLLM locally? Or do we need to convert?
[01:17] Priya: In most cases you can bring the same artifacts — weights and tokenizer. For vLLM there are some runtime patches (like custom attention kernels) that we emulate. For TGI forks it's usually fine but sometimes you need to re-run a small conversion step; it's not usually data-lossy but it's something we test in a benchmark.
[01:35] Lena: What about quantization? We've been experimenting with 4-bit QLoRA-style setups. Does Redwood do quantized inference that preserves eval parity?
[01:44] Priya: We support INT8 and some advanced 4-bit quant paths. The key is that quantization can change model outputs subtly — that's why we do eval parity tests. We can run your eval suite across the candidate quant/profile configs and give a delta report versus your golden outputs.
[02:00] Dina: From security perspective, we need VPC peering, SSO via SAML, KMS integration, and audit logs retained for at least 13 months. Also, any on-prem option?
[02:11] Jordan: Yes we offer Private deployment with customer-managed control plane or an on-prem package for highly regulated customers. Priya: And we integrate with common KMS providers; HSM options are available for the Private model. Audit logs and retention policies are configurable — we can push logs to your SIEM.
[02:30] Markus: Good. One blocker early: we use some custom system messages and rely on token-level deterministic outputs for scoring — worried about covert differences when moving off OpenAI. How do you handle regression detection?
[02:42] Priya: We run regression/eval parity by re-running your eval set across hosted/Dedicated configs. We produce a precision/recall-like breakdown for classification or n-gram/delta metrics for generation. We also do canary rollouts — you can pin model versions and route a portion of traffic to compare.
[03:02] Lena: Can you run the eval on our exact traffic shape? We have a high tail of long-context sequences for a subset of users.
[03:10] Priya: Yes, if you share representative traces and the eval prompts we can replay them. That helps us tune kernel selection and batching for latency.
[03:20] Jordan: Quick qualification — what's your monthly token volume?
[03:23] Markus: Right now, roughly 12B tokens monthly across chat + embeddings; embeddings are ~30% of cost.
[03:31] Jordan: Got it. That volume usually maps to a Dedicated or reserved capacity conversation. We'll run numbers on expected unit cost and tail latency.
[03:38] Markus: Another question — do you support model fallback? For example, if Dedicated capacity hits a limit can we automatically route to Hosted or a lower-cost variant?
[03:47] Priya: Yes, our smart routing supports policy-based fallback: region, cost tier, or model variant. We can automatically degrade to a compatible lower-tier quant model if configured, while recording differences.
[03:58] Lena: And journaling/kv cache — we currently use prefix caching to reduce cost for repeated contexts; does Redwood keep KV cache semantics so we can get similar cost savings?
[04:08] Priya: We do prefix/KV caching and share metrics on cache hit rate. There are implementation differences across runtimes but from an API perspective we keep semantics similar so your app logic doesn't change.
[04:20] Dina: About compliance: do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO stuff we can hand to security? Also penetration test reports?
[04:27] Jordan: We have SOC2 Type II; we can share our security pack. For Dedicated/Private we also provide deployment network diagrams and can sign an MSA with appropriate clauses.
[04:36] Markus: Nice. Ok, can we dive a little into performance? Our P95 latency target is 250ms for short chat turns. With your Dedicated offering, what's realistic?
[04:47] Priya: For short-turn chat on a Dedicated pool with infer-optimized GPUs we typically see p95 under 200-300ms for many models, but it depends on model size and sequence length. For long-context tails we tune batching and KV cache to keep p95 within your SLOs. We can run a representative benchmark.
[05:06] Lena: On the note of benchmarking, we currently run vLLM locally with custom kernels that are very tuned. Will Redwood's kernel selection match that?
[05:14] Priya: We do runtime kernel selection and compile paths based on model arch and sequence shape. It often maps closely to optimized vLLM setups but exact micro-ops differ. The benchmark will show where we align and where adjustments are helpful.
[05:28] Speaker 3: (indistinct) — sorry, background noise — can you talk about pricing model?
[05:33] Jordan: Sure — Hosted is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity with hourly compute + per-token egress adjustments; we'll send a tailored quote given your 12B tokens/month. We can model different quant and batching configs to show unit economics.
[05:48] Markus: Important: embeddings are used heavily and we need vector search throughput. Do you support batching/optimized embedding pipelines?
[05:55] Priya: Yes, embedding pipelines can be batched and optimized; we also support async bulk endpoints for high throughput vectorization. We can also recommend model/quant combos that reduce cost while maintaining embedding quality.
[06:08] Lena: Another technical item: we use a custom tokenizer for some non-English tokens and see tokenization drift across providers. Does Redwood allow custom tokenizers?
[06:17] Priya: We support custom tokenizers in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted you can upload tokenizer bundles and we can validate. Tokenization is one of the primary sources of eval drift, so we pay close attention to that in the parity tests.
[06:31] Dina: Regarding logs and PII — can you guarantee that Hosted endpoints do not persist PII? Or do we need Dedicated/Private for that?
[06:39] Jordan: Hosted has standard retention and is designed for convenience; for stricter PII controls we recommend Dedicated or Private where logs can be routed to your SIEM and retention controlled by policy. We also offer data-at-rest encryption with KMS.
[06:54] Markus: If we start with Hosted to validate integrations and then move to Dedicated, how hard is the migration?
[07:01] Priya: We try to make the API consistent — same endpoints, same SDKs. The main migration work is around capacity planning, tokenization parity, and the eval/quantization steps. We typically propose a pilot: start with a small percentage of traffic, run parity/eval, then ramp to Dedicated.
[07:19] Lena: Are there any customers who've migrated from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated? Any public case studies for similar infra stacks?
[07:26] Jordan: We have anonymized case studies; I'll share links. Several customers with vLLM-based local evaluation have moved to Dedicated for cost reasons.
[07:33] Markus: Ok, let's talk about timeline. We want to decide by end of February. We also have procurement/legal windows for enterprise contracts that could take 4–6 weeks.
[07:42] Jordan: That timeline aligns — we'll aim to get pricing and security docs to you this week so procurement can start early.
[07:50] Priya: Quick technical question for Markus/Lena: what models are you most concerned about parity on? 
[07:55] Lena: Mostly LLaMA-2 variants and a few smaller open-chat models — also a custom fine-tuned instruct model.
[08:02] Priya: Good to know. Fine-tuned instruct models sometimes need extra care for tokenizer or generation hyperparameters — we'll include that in the bench plan.
[08:11] Markus: Another edge: we sometimes run Azure-hosted OpenAI endpoints via enterprise agreements. Any gotchas migrating from Azure OpenAI?
[08:20] Priya: Functionally, the API is similar, but the model variants and versioning are different; we look at sample payloads and the prompt engineering that you use. Sometimes you get small differences in things like stop token behavior. The eval parity run will help detect that.
[08:37] Jordan: I'll capture that as an action item: Priya will run a parity/benchmark against LLaMA-2 and your fine-tuned model.
[08:44] Markus: If we do a Dedicated pilot, what capacity commitment do you normally require?
[08:50] Jordan: It depends on the instance types and expected throughput. For 12B tokens/month, a modest reserved pool is typical; we'll provide a few commitment scenarios in the quote.
[08:59] Dina: A compliance question — do you support SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[09:04] Jordan: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported for enterprise accounts. We'll include setup docs.
[09:11] Lena: About model fallback again — does fallback preserve request metadata so we can attribute cost differences?
[09:17] Priya: Yes, routing metadata and trace IDs are preserved; Redwood Console will show per-route cost and latency.
[09:25] Markus: Great. Any constraints on privacy for Dedicated customers in EU data residency? We have EU users and legal wants logs and data residency guarantees.
[09:34] Jordan: We have regional Dedicated clusters and can pin workloads to regions; Private on-prem is also an option if residency is strict. We'll note the region options in the follow-up.
[09:45] Speaker 2: (brief) — sorry, question on SDKs: do your SDKs match OpenAI's?
[09:49] Jordan: Our SDKs are modeled after common patterns and include helpers for streaming and function calling; we aim for easy migration but there are some Redwood-specific features.
[09:58] Markus: Ok, circling back to eval parity: if parity fails on a quantized config, what's the typical mitigation?
[10:05] Priya: Options are: use a higher-bit quant profile, enable selective layers in fp16, adjust generation hyperparams, or use a fallback to a higher-precision model for critical paths. We quantify quality loss so you can decide tradeoffs.
[10:19] Lena: For our test suite, we need a detailed report showing delta distributions, not just averages.
[10:24] Priya: That's our standard — we provide distributional deltas, per-prompt breakdowns, and example failures.
[10:31] Markus: Let's talk about benchmarks operationally — can you run a load test that simulates our peak concurrency?
[10:37] Priya: Yes, we'll ask for traces and concurrency targets. We'll then run both latency and throughput tests, including embedding bulk runs.
[10:45] Jordan: Quick note — I'll put the links to our security pack and the benchmark intake form in the follow-up email.
[10:52] Dina: Any special NDA or DSAs required for the pilot?
[10:56] Jordan: We can sign a pilot DPA/DSA; procurement will handle that.
[11:01] Markus: Good. I think we have enough for now. Can we summarize next steps?
[11:07] Jordan: Sure. Priya will own the bench run. I'll send pricing and security docs. Markus will share traffic and eval data. We'll tentatively schedule the benchmark week of Jan 19. Does that work?
[11:18] Markus: Works for me.
[11:20] Lena: Works.
[11:21] Dina: Works.
[11:22] Jordan: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the tech deep dive and benchmark intake.
